Q. 68. Are the elect only effectually called?

A. All the elect, and they only, are effectually called; although others may be, and often are, outwardly called by the ministry of the word, and have some common operations of the Spirit; who, for their willful neglect and contempt of the grace offered to them, being justly left in their unbelief, do never truly come to Jesus Christ.

metadata.synopsis: Did a presbytery fail in its duty to condemn erroneous opinions by acquitting a minister on theological-error charges? The SJC denied the complaint, leaving the acquittal undisturbed. A complaint against a not-guilty verdict cannot provoke a retrial at the superior court; under BCO 43 the superior court may only annul or remand, not reverse, and the complainant bore the burden to show error from the record. The record contained the defendant's testimony, including recantations or clarifications, Defense Exhibit 1, and witness testimony sufficient to refrain from contradicting the trial court. The SJC expressly did not decide the defendant's actual views. A separate concurrence elaborated deference standards but did not change the judgment.

metadata.synopsis: Louisiana Presbytery’s refusal to institute process after examining Steve Wilkins’s Federal Vision teachings was challenged for applying the wrong constitutional standard and overlooking a strong presumption that some views were out of conformity with the Westminster Standards. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled Presbytery’s denial. A “difference” need not expressly contradict the Standards; Presbytery must independently investigate and classify it rather than accept the member’s assurance or shift the burden to objectors. The ruling did not adjudicate Wilkins’s guilt; the Central Carolina memorial remained before the SJC.
